questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. The research team is conducting experiments on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease.

The research team is conducting experiments on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease.

options.text: Experiments have been conducted on a new drug that could have revolutionised the treatment of the disease through the research team.
options.html: Experiments have been conducted on a new drug that could have revolutionised the treatment of the disease through the research team.

options.text: Experiments are being conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease by the research team.
options.html: Experiments are being conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease by the research team.

questions.solution:
· The active voice sentence is in present continuous tense ("is conducting").

· To convert it to passive voice, we follow the structure:

Object + is/are being + past participle + by + subject

· Option 4 correctly follows this structure:

"Experiments are being conducted on a new drug that could revolutionise the treatment of the disease by the research team."

· Option 1 changes the tense incorrectly.

· Option 2 uses past continuous, which is incorrect.

· Option 3 has an incorrect structure and wording.

Thus, option 4 is the correct answer.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. My dog / barks / very louder / at night.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

My dog / barks / very louder / at night.
questions.solution:
The phrase "very louder" is incorrect because "louder" is the comparative form of "loud," and comparative adjectives should not take the word "very" for intensification. Instead, we use "much louder" or "very loud."

Correct sentence:

"My dog barks much louder at night."

· Option 1 (My dog) - Correct, as it is the subject of the sentence.

· Option 3 (Barks) - Correct verb form for present simple tense.

· Option 4 (At night) - Correct prepositional phrase indicating time.

Hence, option 2 ("very louder") is the incorrect segment.
